children: NITI Aayog reportedly shortlists Central Bank of India and Indian Overseas Bank as potential candidates for privatisation

The Centre is considering reducing its shareholding in four public sector banks to 75 per cent to meet minimum public shareholding requirements, while preparing for another round of consolidation among state-owned lenders, according to media reports.

The banks under consideration are Central Bank of India, UCO Bank, Punjab & Sind Bank and Indian Overseas Bank. The government could also identify two more lenders for privatisation as part of its broader plan to reshape the public sector banking landscape, the reports said.
The move follows the government's announcement in the Union Budget for 2021-22 that it would privatise two public sector banks and one general insurance company, in addition to IDBI Bank.
Earlier this month, the government announced that Fairfax Financial Holdings, promoted by Canadian billionaire Prem Watsa, would acquire a 60.72 per cent stake in IDBI Bank for Rs 52,878 crore.

The government's longer-term objective is to create three to four large public sector banks, according to the reports. NITI Aayog had reportedly shortlisted Central Bank of India and Indian Overseas Bank as potential candidates for privatisation.
In the immediate term, the Centre is prioritising an increase in public shareholding in the four lenders over the next year, a newspaper report cited an official as saying.

The banks could raise capital from the market based on their individual funding strategies. The government may also consider selling part of its holdings through offers for sale, depending on prevailing market conditions.
Increasing the public float could also help improve the valuation of these lenders by expanding the proportion of shares available for trading, the report said.
Legislative Changes May Be Needed For Privatisation

The proposed privatisation exercise would require legislative amendments, including changes to the Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act. These amendments could be pursued alongside the bank consolidation process, according to the report.

The government had exempted state-owned companies, including financial institutions, from the minimum public shareholding requirement of 25 per cent until August 2026. A further extension is expected to be notified, the reports said.

The IDBI Bank transaction has also highlighted the government's approach to valuation during disinvestment. During the privatisation process, the government clarified that the bank's volatile share price, amid limited trading activity, was not considered representative of its intrinsic enterprise value, according to media reports.
